segments: ... and the falsehood and arrogance of the Arabs were greatly revealed to him,
and that whatever they do,
they do with deceit and hypocrisy.
And immediately he commanded
that Sa'd al-Dawlah the Jew,
who had been governor in Baghdad,
should become the head of the scribes,
that is, the Sahib Diwan,
in the whole realm of his kingdom,
and that Arab scribes should not be appointed anywhere at all,
but Christians and Jews alone.
And thus again the hatred and malice of the Arabs {error for Muslims} grew fierce.
And consequently, when that Jew was put in authority
and the administration of the realm was delivered to him,
he sent his brother as governor in Baghdad in his place.
And his other brother, together with Taj al-Din bar Mukhtass, the supreme commissioner, he sent to Mosul, Mardin, and all Diyar Bakr.
And when these men arrived in these regions,
a certain Kurdish emir, who for a long time had been governor in Erbil,
who was known as Mubariz al-Din Kawkbag {OCR?},
feared them.
And he thought that these men were about to inflict evils upon him,
and he quickly and speedily sought the road to the royal camp.
For he said,
"When I appear with a compassionate eye before the King of Kings,
every kind of fear will be removed from me."
And when he had thus gone,
those emirs also sent many accusers after him against him.
The King of Kings intended to kill him,
yet in the meantime he kept him in suspense with hope.
And he secretly sent a messenger
that they should first seize his sons, his household, and the members of his race and family,
so that he might destroy them completely,
and then they should kill him who was with them, in their hands.
Now a certain woman who had become aware of this secret
came to the Kurdish emir by night,
and informed him of the whole matter.
The Kurd, then, without delay, at that very hour took one of his servants,
and the two of them mounted and fled from the camp,
and they escaped like a bird from the snare.
And all this he flew swiftly on horses,
so that he arrived ahead of that messenger.
And he reached his home,
and he caused his family and all his provisions to escape {OCR?},
and he took refuge in the mountains, the heights, and impregnable steep places.
And after this the messenger arrived, confounded and amazed {OCR?}.
Then the King of Kings was inflamed with wrath and blazed up.
